evidence.clarity: 390 and 1440: headline 'What close needs to tell open.' only makes sense to someone who already says 'close' and 'open', but the next line ('a shared logbook for restaurant managers. What ran out, who called in sick, what needs fixing — written at the end of one shift, read on a phone at the start of the next') says what it is, who it is for and when it is used. The next step is 'Start a free trial', with the line 'Takes you to app.shiftnote.example to sign up.' under it.
evidence.fit: Keeps the name, logo.svg and both brand colours (indigo buttons, coral tags and margin rule). Drops the fake 'trusted by' names and testimonials. All three 'Start a free trial' links (header, hero, closing) go to https://app.shiftnote.example/signup, and the hero and closing ones state the destination. The phone manager is served well. The owner who pays gets one step card ('Sunday night / The owner reads the whole week') and nothing they can see, which is a token path for the person holding the budget.
evidence.distinctiveness: The artifact is a ruled logbook page with a coral margin line, times written in the margin and serif 'handwriting' entries. The 'What goes in the log' list reuses the same ruled-paper motif. With the logo removed you would still read it as a handover book. The overall structure (hero, three steps, list, 'why not X', CTA band) is still familiar.
evidence.proof: 1440 and 390: the 'Example handover' (Tuesday close for Wednesday open, written by Dani at 11:48 pm) is in the first screen. Its four entries read like real service ('86’d the halibut', 'Table 14 wobbles — there’s a wedge under it for now') and are consistent with the step times (11:48 pm). It is static, so it shows what goes in but not what the opener or owner does with it.
evidence.craft: Clean type scale and spacing at 1440, 768 and 390, and probe shows no overflow or axe violations. Minor issues: at 1440 there is a large empty area under the hero CTA in the left column, and the log card runs about 4 empty ruled lines past its last entry.
evidence.mobile: 390: headline, lead, full CTA with its destination note, the 'Read an example handover' link and the labelled example header all fit in the first screen. The sticky header keeps 'Start a free trial' in view. I tapped 'Read an example handover' and it scrolled to the log (scrollY 551). The page is short (4294px). The header CTA is 40px tall, under 44. On phones the section nav is hidden and there is no menu, which is acceptable with this few sections.
evidence.honesty: The artifact is labelled 'Example handover' at its top in every width, including 390. Each main button states where it goes before you tap. The closing section says 'No logos to show you. No case studies yet.' and then gives a concrete thing to try, which reads as confident rather than apologetic. 'Free' trial is not stated in the brief, which only says trials start at the URL; B says the same. The four entry 'marks' are presented as product fact without support in the brief.
evidence.interaction: Every control is a link and all of them work: the hero CTA at 390 and 1440 navigated to https://app.shiftnote.example/signup, 'How it works' scrolled to #how (scrollY 1005 at 1440), 'Read an example handover' jumped to #example at 390, and a skip link appears on Tab. There is nothing to operate in the artifact, so you cannot try writing or reading an entry, and there are no states to test.
evidence.copy: Specific, restaurant-native and short: 'The group chat scrolls away. The sticky note falls off the screen. The binder stays at the host stand, where the closer isn’t and the owner never is.' 'That’s the whole product.' No buzzwords. Button text and destination notes are consistent. The headline is a little oblique for someone arriving cold.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: headline, lead, CTA plus destination note, and a labelled example handover with four entries are all in one viewport. 390: headline, lead, CTA with note, and the example header plus its first entry are in view. The promise is specific to managers. Nothing in view speaks to the owner.

problems: The owner who pays gets only one three-line step card ('The owner reads the whole week') and no picture of what they would see on the laptop.
The example handover is static, so a manager cannot see what reading or acting on an entry looks like the next morning.
The headline 'What close needs to tell open.' is clever but abstract; the specific promise sits in the lead line rather than the headline.

evidence.clarity: 1440 and 390: the headline 'Nothing from tonight’s close gets lost by tomorrow’s open.' is a concrete outcome. The lead says it is a shift logbook for restaurant managers, written on a phone at close and read first thing by whoever opens. The CTA 'Start a free trial' has 'Opens the signup page at app.shiftnote.example. No sales call; you set it up yourself.' beside it. The lead is long: one sentence with a semicolon.
evidence.fit: Keeps the name, logo and both colours: indigo buttons and handled state, coral 'Open' dots. The fake names and testimonials are gone, and every 'Start a free trial' (header, hero, menu, closing, footer) goes to the brief's signup URL with the destination stated. Each audience gets its own path: the closer (Step 1 composer), the opener (Step 2 'Sam opened the note') and the owner (Step 3 'Week of 13 Oct' table, which stacks into cards at 390). 'What stays out' (POS, schedules, payroll) answers the 'another system?' worry. It presents per-item owners and a 'Mark handled' workflow as product features, which the brief does not mention.
evidence.distinctiveness: A ticket/docket look with mono timestamps, boxed uppercase tags and a serif headline. Every artifact (close note, composer, opener view, owner week) is the product itself rather than decoration. The page skeleton (hero, numbered steps with art on the right, list plus aside, CTA) is a familiar template, and there is no single motif as recognisable as a logbook page.
evidence.proof: 1440: the operable close note sits beside the headline. At 390 it starts in the first screen, and the first 'Mark handled' is at y=975. Its numbers are internally consistent: 2 open items in the note, 'Sam opened the note · 2 open items', and the owner week shows '5 closes · 2 still open' with two open rows. Weak spot: the timestamps the demo creates use the visitor's real clock, so at 390 marking the walk-in handled showed 'Handled · Sam, 11:35 am' and a composer entry in the 10:52 pm close was stamped '11:35 am · Priya M.'.
evidence.craft: Consistent tokens, clear hierarchy and no overflow or axe violations at 1440, 768 or 390. Body text is a lighter grey that reads a little faint. The page is dense: 4430px at 1440 and 6699px at 390.
evidence.mobile: 390: the 'Menu' toggle opens a stacked panel with a full-width trial button and closes on Escape and on link tap. The hero CTA is full-width at 48px. The close note starts inside the first screen, and the owner table recomposes into cards. Against that, the page is 6699px long, and 'Mark handled', the chips and 'Add to tonight’s note' are 40px tall (under 44). The sample label for the hero note is under the whole note, roughly two screens down.
evidence.honesty: Sample labels exist: a caption under the note ('The restaurant and the people are made up; nothing you press here is saved or sent'), a hint by the composer ('Sample only; nothing is sent'), 'Sample week' under the table, and a footer line. At 390, though, the hero note's header just says 'Close note' and its sample caption is about two screens below, so the label is late. The page states 'every item keeps an owner until it’s handled' and shows a handled/owner workflow as fact, beyond what the brief supports. The absence-of-customers line appears in both hero and footer. 'Free' is not in the brief, the same as A.
evidence.interaction: At 390 I tapped 'Mark handled' on the walk-in: the state changed to 'Handled · Sam, 11:35 am', the button became 'Undo', and Undo restored 'Open · Sam, opening Wed'. Keyboard Enter on the button at 1440 also worked. I picked the 'Repair' chip and tapped 'Add to tonight’s note': the entry landed under 'Tonight’s note so far', the empty message hid, and the input refilled with a new suggestion. Pressing Enter in the input also adds. On empty input, 'Write something first.' goes only to a screen-reader live region; visually only focus moves. A 400-character unbroken string pushed 1830px of horizontal overflow at 390, while a realistic long sentence wrapped fine. No console errors. The CTA navigated to the signup URL.
evidence.copy: Mostly specific and in the customer's own words: 'Deposit bag is in the safe, not dropped.', 'Walk-ins, dish machines, heaters, the one toilet.', 'What was promised, so it gets kept.', and button labels say what they do. Some sentences are heavy or clunky: 'One note, written once, read by three people who need different things from it.' and 'The note is built so a close takes about as long as a text thread, with none of the scrolling.'
evidence.first_screen: 1440: specific outcome headline, lead, CTA with destination note, an operable sample note, and a line saying the note is a sample. 390: headline, lead, full-width CTA with note, and the top of the note are in view, but nothing in view says it is a sample and no 'Mark handled' button is visible yet.

problems: The hero copy and demo present per-item owners and 'Mark handled' as product features the brief never mentions; if the app doesn't do this, the page overpromises to a buyer who will find out in the trial.
On a phone the page is long (6699px at 390), the hero note's sample label sits about two screens below its header, and the tap targets in the demo are 40px.
Demo timestamps use the visitor's clock ('Handled · Sam, 11:35 am', a 10:52 pm close entry stamped '11:35 am'), and the empty-input error is invisible to sighted users.

reason: Both pages are honest, specific and well executed for the manager on a phone. B also gives the owner who pays a real path: the week view with who owned each item and what is still open is the argument that gets a budget approved, while A gives the owner three lines. A has the tighter copy, the shorter phone read and the earlier sample label. I would switch to A if B's handled/owner workflow is not actually in the product, because then B's best argument is a promise the trial cannot keep.
